triage.note: The counterpart PR #21 R1/R2/R3 established: a check that asserts the real file is clean also passes vacuously once it regresses, so a known-bad fixture has to prove the miss is actually caught. Eight mutations, eleven failures, exact count — the checkbox carries two independent defects (`checked` and `disabled`) on one element — `min_failures` alone is a floor and would let a regressed check that ALSO over-fires report green (PR #21 round-2 R5). The shapes are listed in the fixture's own header comment; the two that matter most are the checked-and-disabled checkbox (a paid tier as the deployed default, on a control nobody can untick) and a `routingStrip` that is declared, is never called from the banner, and prints no cost — the demo's own failure shape, a number computed and not shown, moved one layer up. PR #58 R6 added shape 7 and three of the ten: a page that offers the escalate box unconditionally — never asking the server whether it is armed, never disabling the control, never rendering the server's refusal — is a tickable box whose value is silently discarded on an unarmed deployment. With a real credential about to land on a public, unauthenticated host, that is the shape most worth catching. PR #58 R17/R19 added shape 8 and the eleventh: a strip with no truncation clause at all. Its predecessor clause was worse than absent — it said 'the first N chars' about rung 1's window, which starts at the largest unattributed region and on 18 of 43 dev documents does not start at 0, so the screen stated a falsehood the envelope could not even contradict (no offset was published). The pin therefore requires the RANGE, read from the record's own `offset`, not a length.

provenance: D11, created 2026-08-26 alongside the check it falsifies, per hard rule 2. Extended 2026-08-27 in the PR #58 round-1 repair with the arming shape; count 7 -> 10. Extended 2026-08-27 (PR #58 round 3) with the truncation-clause shape; count 10 -> 11.
